title: Evaluating RAG: Hit-Rate to Honesty
objective: After this lesson you will be able to score retrieval (hit-rate, MRR), generation (faithfulness, citation coverage, abstention precision), combine them into severity-weighted gates, and taxonomize failures by stage for targeted fixes.
why: 'The demo looked good' ships incidents: retrieval misses hide behind fluent answers, stale prices average into great hit-rates, one severity class poisons the whole. RAG eval separates retrieval truth (found the gold?) from generation truth (said only sourced things?) with per-stage metrics and severity weights — the measurement spine of the capstone.

blocks.text: **Hit-rate@k**: fraction of questions with a gold chunk in top-k (binary per question, averaged). **MRR** (mean reciprocal rank): 1/rank of the first gold hit, averaged — rewards top placement, not just presence. Track both: hit-rate gates coverage ('found at all'), MRR gates ordering quality ('found first'). Slice by query kind (SKU vs paraphrase vs vague) — aggregate scores hide the segments that need different fixes.

blocks.caption: Two retrieval numbers: found-at-all vs found-first

blocks.text: **Faithfulness**: every claim entailed by cited spans (sampled human or NLI-model judged). **Citation coverage**: % factual claims carrying citations (mechanical check). **Abstention precision**: unknowns truly absent vs answerable-but-missed (gold-labeled). Plus **staleness violations**: money claims past max-age (zero-tolerance counter, never averaged).

Not all misses price equally: price errors >> policy vagueness >> chitchat gaps. **Severity-weighted gates**: money claims require 100% grounding enforcement (hard gate — any violation blocks ship); general hit-rate targets 0.85+; chitchat untracked. A 9/10 with the miss on $500 fails; 8/10 all-benign passes with notes. Averages never overrule severity.

blocks.caption: Vetoes → segments → bars: gating order reflects severity order

blocks.title: Score the runs
blocks.note: Run it: expect hitRate 0.75, mrr 0.63 (ranks 1,2,miss,1 → 1 + 1/2 + 0 + 1 = 2.5/4 hits... verify: hits at rank<2: c1 rank0 ✓, c2 rank1 ✓, c3 miss, c4 rank0 ✓ → 3/4 = 0.75; mrr (1 + 0.5 + 0 + 1)/4 = 0.625 → 0.63). Then gates: money violation vetoes despite 0.9; clean ships.

items: Retrieval: hit-rate (coverage) + MRR (placement), sliced by query kind
Generation: faithfulness + citation coverage + abstention precision + zero-tolerance staleness counter
Gates: money vetoes → weak segments → aggregate bars; severity overrules averages

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice scorer and confirm 0.75/0.63 with per-run rank mapping. (b) Change k to 1 and recompute by hand; state what k-choice measures (coverage depth vs top precision). (c) Write the ship verdicts for: {0.9, 1 violation} vs {0.8, 0 violations} — and defend the counterintuitive one.
hints: k=1: only rank-0 hits count → c1, c4 → 0.5 hit-rate; MRR same numerator over... recompute: (1+0+0+1)/4 = 0.5. k trades coverage depth for top precision.
0.9+violation → NO SHIP (veto); 0.8 clean → NO SHIP (below bar) — both blocked, different reasons; severity and bars are independent gates.
exercise.why: k-sensitivity (what the parameter measures), dual-block verdicts (vetoes AND bars independently), and rank mapping make metrics operational rather than ornamental.
exercise.code: // Metric-sensitivity pattern: vary k, watch what the number starts measuring.

options: Found eventually but rarely first — ordering/rerank problem, not coverage: fix ranking, not recall
quiz.explain: High coverage + low placement = ordering failure. The fix is reranking/ordering, never broader recall.

quiz.q: 9/10 hit-rate, the miss is a $500 price. Ship?
options: No: money violations veto regardless of averages — severity-weighted gates overrule hit-rates
quiz.explain: Severity gates: money grounding is binary (100% enforced), not averaged. One price hallucination outweighs nine good answers.

quiz.q: Right doc retrieved, unsupported answer. First investigation?
options: Generation: scope/citation/position — context present but unused means consumer failure
quiz.explain: Right-doc-wrong-answer exonerates retrieval. Investigate grounding contracts, citation enforcement, and context assembly.

summary: Hit-rate + MRR (sliced), faithfulness triple + staleness veto, severity-ordered gates. Measure retrieval and generation separately; gate by severity, never averages.
next: Measured stages need orchestration across needs: routers, multi-hop loops, and escalation. Next: agentic RAG.
